Package io.mavlink4j.codec

Interface FrameSink

public interface FrameSink
Frames out — the one public TX door. Sequence numbering, our own sysid/compid stamping, signing and framing are all handled by the implementation; callers hand over a message and where it should go. A message is a dialect message class (for example CommandLong): the dialect model has no common supertype, hence Object.

Thread-safety: Implementations must be thread-safe: services on several threads send through one sink.

      void send(Object message, PeerId target)
      Sends message addressed to target, on the link it was last heard on and to the address it was last heard at.
      Parameters:
      message - a dialect message object — see FrameWriter for the validation applied

      Throws:

    • broadcastAll

      default void broadcastAll(Object message)
      Broadcasts message on every link in links() — how a heartbeat reaches a dial-out link nobody has spoken on yet. Goes through broadcast(java.lang.Object, io.mavlink4j.transport.LinkId), so any gate a wrapping sink applies per link applies here too. Best effort per link: a link that cannot be addressed yet (a listen link that has heard nothing, so has no learned target) is logged and skipped, it never stops the others.
